solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Nick's fresh debacle which has one open-mouthed

indicators.note: a debacle is a collapse into chaos, so the preceding words fall apart and are put back together differently

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, letters taken as printed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick suffers a cheeky embarrassment that leaves a person gaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' reads as cheeky in the surface, but it simply joins Nick's as letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, tongue-led kiss is performed with lips parted, so the phrase describes it playfully as something done with mouth agape.

clue.text: Better backing, er, female alternative over male!

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the little word after it is read from its end to its start

parts.note: the hesitation word, written backwards
F is the standard abbreviation for female
or is the word that introduces an alternative
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A sly suggestion that swapping a man for a woman would improve things.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the male letter comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to improve something means to amend or correct it, the same sense as changing it for the good.

clue.text: Less feeling — figure it's no place for Miliband

parts.note: more numb, i.e. having less sensation
a number, or figure

explanation.surface: A jibe that Ed Miliband, numbed by defeat, will never reach the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less feeling' looks like a noun phrase but is the comparative of numb. Ed Miliband led Labour to defeat in 2015, so never lived at 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister's official London residence is Downing Street's tenth house, which the defeated Labour leader never got to occupy.

clue.text: Daring the woman with "Hey, S&M!"

parts.note: the pronoun for a woman
oi is a British call to get attention, like hey
the two letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A woman greets someone with a bold invitation to sadomasochism.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and boldness in the face of danger is what daring means as a noun, the quality of a brave person.

clue.text: Violet's one doing splits

indicators.note: splitting apart breaks the preceding words into bits that can be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman called Violet shows off her gymnastic splits.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet looks like a girl's name; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep blue-purple colour sits beside its neighbour in the rainbow, and dictionaries treat it as a shade close to purple.

clue.text: Resign if you're mean inside

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the run of words before it, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A curt instruction to quit if you are a miserly or nasty person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like the adjective nasty but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate or denote something is to convey a sense, the verb meaning carry a particular sense.

clue.text: see 28ac.
Like Hampstead's head's cover lacking on top?

indicators.note: lacking on top means missing what sits uppermost, so the opening letter is lost

parts.note: a wrapped cloth worn over the head

explanation.surface: Hints at a balding Hampstead headmaster losing the hair on his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampstead is a well-to-do district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Being part of a city, Hampstead is a metropolitan district rather than a rural one, which describes the town character.

clue.text: Temperature taken inside Dolly's bust — ultimately quite quaint

indicators.note: taken inside means placed within, so one piece goes into the middle of another
something bust is broken, so the letters of the preceding word are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, letters taken as printed
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone's temperature is checked under Dolly's bosom, which seems rather old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' reads as a bosom in the surface; it is the signal for breaking up the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasingly old-fashioned is quaint, the hyphenated adjective describing a manner belonging to an earlier era.

clue.text: Gaffe: Murdoch reveals part of member

indicators.note: to reveal is to expose something already there, here letters concealed within the adjacent words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about Rupert Murdoch blundering and exposing part of a body, perhaps a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP or a rude body part; here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone is the long bone of the leg, and a leg is a limb or member of the body.

clue.text: Rogue southern corporation's doormat

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible fellow, a scoundrel
S is the abbreviation for southern
a body is an organised group, such as a corporation

explanation.surface: A crooked southern company is a walkover for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: A dogsbody is British slang for a drudge who does menial chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge given menial jobs is put upon like a doormat, the figurative term for someone others walk over.

clue.text: Low-down conduct surrounding "Inflexibly English" Farage's origins

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to conduct someone is to bring them along

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so each of the preceding words contributes only its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: Low conduct around Nigel Farage, painted as stubbornly English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-down' looks like an adjective for base behaviour but is the noun for information. Nigel Farage is the British anti-EU politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-down is informal for the inside facts, and a briefing is a session where such facts are passed on.

clue.text: Kindle: after getting leg over, it turns to jelly

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the limb word is read from end to start
the answer becomes the explosive only after it gains a prefix, so the explosive minus that prefix is what we want

parts.note: jelly is slang for the explosive gelignite
taken as written, then flipped

explanation.surface: A smutty tale of someone's legs turning to jelly after a sexual conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, leg gives the three letters which, put in front of the answer, make gelignite, the explosive known as jelly. 'Kindle' also suggests the e-reader.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle a fire is to set it alight, start it burning, so the two verbs mean the same thing.

clue.text: see 28ac.
Parliament's time before (yawn) sad Liberal Democrats vastly reduced

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: sad here means sorry or wretched, the state of something knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the party's name cut down to the initials used in election results

explanation.surface: A weary verdict on Parliament, where the Liberal Democrats have been cut to a rump.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats were reduced from 57 seats to 8 in 2015. The Isle of Man's parliament is an ancient assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tynwald is the legislature of the Isle of Man, claimed to be the oldest continuous parliamentary body in the world.

clue.text: Empty talk by members about Farage's capital energy sources

indicators.note: about means around, so the combined words go around the single letter

parts.note: wind is idle or boastful talk
arms are limbs, or members

indicators.note: a capital is a head or top letter, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Mocks members prattling about Nigel Farage's money, or his capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Farage, the anti-EU politician, opposed onshore turbine farms.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of turbines harness moving air to generate electricity, making them renewable sources of power.

clue.text: Obit (Amin): pathetic object

indicators.note: pathetic means feeble and in a sorry state, so the bracketed words are reduced to a jumble

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An obituary for Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator, dismissed as a pitiful thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a thing, but here it means a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: An object in the sense of aim or purpose is a goal one strives for, which is what an ambition is.

clue.text: Exalted, those people commonly elected to attend hospital

parts.note: 'em is the colloquial form of them
a candidate elected is in
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: Prestigious people, once voted in, turn up to a hospital visit.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent person is distinguished and of high rank, raised above others, which matches exalted in standing.

clue.text: Has the low-down on reported task of nozzle modification

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the phrase is what counts

parts.note: to have the low-down on something is to know about it
a job is a task

explanation.surface: Someone has inside information about a reported assignment involving a nozzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Nozzle is slang for the human nose, so changing its shape is cosmetic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, cosmetic surgery to reshape the hooter, is jokingly a modification of one's conk.

clue.text: Shag on, youth — it covers the pain

indicators.note: covers means conceals, so the letters are tucked away in the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Urging a young man to keep going at sex, since it masks his suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony means extreme suffering, physical or mental, so it is a strong word for intense hurt.

clue.text: Noble fellow shagged after grand party

indicators.note: after places the slangy verb behind the lavish occasion, so the clue's second piece comes first

parts.note: a gala is a grand festive occasion
slang: to have someone is to have sex with them

explanation.surface: A man of rank beds someone after a lavish do.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue order puts the conquest first, but 'after' places it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the pure knight of Arthurian legend, stands for any chivalrous, honourable man.

clue.text: Female resistance against old man who's expert on mounts

parts.note: the female pronoun
R is the physics symbol for resistance
pa is a father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A woman resists her father, a skilled horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounts' suggests horses; it means mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan people famed as guides and porters are expert at climbing mountains, abbreviated as mounts.

clue.text: Renewed Cameron not working — stifling independence, creating a war zone

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the letters close around the next piece
renewed means made over afresh, so the remaining letters are rebuilt in a new order
working can be the little word on, so 'not working' asks for that to be taken away

parts.note: the name taken as written
I is the abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A revived David Cameron, ineffective and crushing independence, starts a war.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the letters for working from the name leaves CAMER, which takes in I before being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea peninsula was the scene of the 1850s war and of Russia's 2014 annexation, so it is a conflict region.

clue.text: Wealth of birds dumping pervy sot

indicators.note: pervy means perverted, twisted, so the drunkard's letters are bent into another order
dumping means getting rid of, so those letters are dropped from the birds

parts.note: large flightless birds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Women ditching a sleazy drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds' is British slang for young women in the surface; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches are great amounts of money or valuable possessions, so the plural noun is a synonym of wealth.

clue.text: Points not accepted by this speedy politician

definitions.text: Points not accepted by this speedy politician

parts.words: Points not accepted by this speedy politician
parts.note: surface: a quick-thinking politician who rejects arguments put to him
setter's reading: a minister caught speeding who refused to take the penalty points on his licence

explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrat cabinet minister was jailed in 2013 for getting his wife to accept his speeding points. In Britain, points go on a driving licence for motoring offences.
explanation.definitionFit: The disgraced former Energy Secretary dodged driving penalty points by passing them to his then wife, a scandal that ended his career.

clue.text: Damnation! What will Sugar do?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an oath, and the eternal torment of the damned
second meaning, split into he'll and fire: what Lord Sugar does to failed candidates

explanation.walkthrough: Lord Alan Sugar is the businessman who ends each episode of the British TV show The Apprentice by telling someone 'You're fired'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flames of hell are eternal punishment, and the word is also used as an exclamation like damn; read as two words it predicts Sugar sacking someone.

clue.text: Flier's thing managed to give an unpleasant shock

indicators.note: managed here means manipulated or handled, so the word before it is reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to jar is to jolt or shake unpleasantly

explanation.surface: A pilot's gadget gives someone a nasty jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird, and any bird can be called a flier in crosswords.

clue.text: Group of wives wants hot member with electronic insert

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: an insert is something put inside, so this letter goes into the limb

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A polygamous household wants a sexy man with a battery-powered implant.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a polygamous household, the wives and concubines of one man.

clue.text: (& 7ac./13ac.) How Cinderella gets a start, seeing a Mountie ponce around!

indicators.note: around means turned about and moved here and there, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: Cinderella's story starts when she spots a Canadian policeman preening about.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mountie is a Royal Canadian Mounted policeman; a ponce is British slang for an effeminate show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales such as Cinderella traditionally open with this stock phrase, so it is how her story begins.

clue.text: You can get your teeth into this book with sexy pic

definitions.text: You can get your teeth into this

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
randy is British slang for lustful
a snap is a snapshot, a photo

explanation.surface: A book with racy photos that a reader can really get stuck into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your teeth into' sounds like the idiom for a meaty read, but it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp, rolled ginger biscuit is a treat literally bitten, so the idiom for engaging with something becomes a literal description.
